evidence.label: a.md
evidence.text:
19/100 → 82/100 in about 3 minutes, unattended.

Claude Code took an AI one-shot dashboard and rebuilt it on GitHub's Primer design system until Verdict passed it. 17-second video below.

Which design system would you test your agent against?

evidence.label: brief.md
evidence.text:
# What the post announces (facts the post may use)
- A 17-second screen recording: Claude Code on the left, a dashboard on the right.
- The dashboard started as an AI one-shot: dark purple glow, glass cards. Verdict scored it 19/100 against GitHub's
  open-source Primer design system.
- The agent installed Primer, ran an importer that turned Primer's tokens (751 colours, a 7-step type scale, spacing,
  radii, component classes) into a Verdict rubric, and rebuilt the page.
- Scores: 19 → 76 → 82 (passes at 80). Every colour, size and spacing value on the final page is a Primer token.
- About 3 minutes, unattended. The data is fictional.
- Verdict is an evaluation engine: rubrics scored by decision models, humans and deterministic checks.
- Audience: developers and designers on X who use coding agents.
